content.fullText: You are at the center of the Earth. The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel the size of the Moon. Despite temperatures over 5,000°C, the extreme pressure keeps it solid. It's a crystal in a hellish furnace.
content.logicBonus: If the pressure suddenly vanished but the heat stayed, what would happen to the core? (Hint: Phase change).

questions.q: Why is the inner core solid despite the extreme heat?
a: Crushing pressure prevents atoms from moving
questions.hint: Think about what happens to ice when you press it very hard.

content.fullText: The outer core is liquid. Earth's rotation stirs the molten iron like a giant blender, creating electric currents. This generates our magnetic field—an invisible shield protecting us from lethal cosmic radiation. Without it, Earth would be a dead desert like Mars.
content.logicBonus: A compass points North. If the outer core stopped spinning, what would happen to your phone's GPS?

questions.q: What would happen to Earth's atmosphere if the core completely cooled down and solidified?
a: Solar winds would slowly blow it away into space
questions.hint: The magnetic field works like an umbrella in a storm of solar particles.

content.fullText: The ground looks solid, but you are floating. Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates moving at the speed your fingernails grow. They crash to build mountains (Himalayas) or pull apart to create new oceans.
content.logicBonus: India was once an island near Africa. It 'sailed' north until it hit Asia. What happened to the seafloor that was between them?

questions.q: Sea fossils are found on top of Mt. Everest (8,848m). How is this possible?
a: Ocean levels were once that high
Old seafloor was pushed up by colliding continents
questions.hint: Continents work like giant bulldozers, pushing everything in front of them.

content.fullText: At 4,000 meters deep, the pressure is like having an elephant stand on your thumb. There is no sunlight, so plants can't grow. Instead, life thrives around hydrothermal vents—underwater volcanoes—using chemicals instead of sun for energy. This is called chemosynthesis.
content.logicBonus: Red light doesn't reach the deep ocean. If a fish is bright red down there, what color does it appear to a predator? (Black / Bright Red / White).

questions.q: How do deep-sea creatures survive without sunlight?
a: They use chemical energy from vents
They swim to the surface every night

content.fullText: The atmosphere isn't just air; it's a multi-layered shield. The Ozone layer blocks UV rays that would burn our DNA, while the Mesosphere acts as a 'shooting gallery' where meteors burn up before hitting the ground. You are currently protected by a thin skin of gases.
content.logicBonus: Most commercial planes fly at 10km (Troposphere boundary). Why is the air so much colder there than on the ground if they are closer to the Sun?

questions.q: Which layer of the atmosphere is responsible for burning up most meteors?

content.fullText: The Moon is our only natural satellite. Its gravity tugs on Earth's oceans, creating tides. But it also stabilizes Earth's wobble, keeping our climate steady. Interestingly, the Moon moves 3.8cm away from Earth every year. One day, it will look much smaller in our sky.
content.logicBonus: If you weigh 100kg on Earth, you weigh only 16kg on the Moon. Is it because you lost mass, or because gravity is weaker?
